clue.text: Often does badly, but gets decorated

indicators.note: doing something badly gets it wrong, so the two words before it are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone who often performs poorly is nonetheless honoured with a medal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges the nine letters of OFTEN DOES; 'but gets' only joins. 'decorated' looks like medals, but the sense is hung with garlands.
explanation.definitionFit: To festoon is to hang garlands or chains of ornament on something, so the past participle means adorned.

clue.text: A carrier going from one bank to another

definitions.text: A carrier going from one bank to another

parts.words: A carrier going from one bank to another
parts.note: bank seems financial, as with a cash carrier, but it is the bank of a river, crossed by a vessel taking passengers

explanation.definitionFit: This vessel shuttles passengers and vehicles across a river or strait.

clue.text: Roman dictator given total American backing

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the two pieces before it are read in reverse

parts.note: all means the total or whole

explanation.surface: A Roman strongman receives full support from the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns ALLUS into SULLA; 'given' only links. 'backing' looks like support but signals the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucius Cornelius Sulla seized power in ancient Rome and ruled as dictator around 81 BC.

clue.text: Take work modelling, though it's not in agreement

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
posing is what a model does

explanation.surface: Someone takes a modelling job despite disagreeing with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take' and 'though it's' only link. OP is opus, Latin for a work.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposing sides are contrary or at odds, so they disagree.

clue.text: Sewers, a quarter being superfluous

parts.note: a sewer here is one who sews, and needles are things that sew
S for south is one of the four compass quarters

explanation.surface: Drains, a quarter of which are surplus to need.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sewers' looks like drains but is read as things that sew.
explanation.definitionFit: Something superfluous is unnecessary, not required at all.

clue.text: Plain-spoken guide

explanation.surface: A tour leader who speaks frankly.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank, straightforward speech is the adjective sense; to steer or manage someone's course is the verb sense.

clue.text: Like a little house here?

parts.note: as means like, in the sense of in the manner of
a cot is an old word for a small cottage

explanation.surface: A question about whether this is the spot for something resembling a tiny cottage.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is just 'here?': ASCOT is the Berkshire racecourse, scene of the famous Royal Ascot meeting; the question mark flags that the place is pointed at, not described.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue points at a place, and Ascot is an English town known for its royal racecourse.

clue.text: A famous physicist — and a politician before

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: Describing a great scientist who once had a career in politics.
explanation.walkthrough: André-Marie Ampère was the French physicist after whom the unit of electric current is named.
explanation.definitionFit: André-Marie Ampère was a French pioneer of electromagnetism, honoured by the unit of current.

clue.text: Awfully curt cad or knave perhaps

indicators.note: awfully means very badly, so the letters of the three following words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Calling someone a terribly rude bounder, or perhaps a rogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knave' reads as a rogue with 'cad', but it is the jack in a pack of cards; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A jack, also called a knave, is one of the picture cards in a pack alongside king and queen.

clue.text: Hair in distressing condition

indicators.note: in shows the letters sit inside the longer word that follows

explanation.surface: Hair in a sorry state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'condition' only links, though it looks like part of a hair-care phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A lock or curl of long hair is called this, a poetic word for a ringlet.

clue.text: A reason for ill-feeling yet again

definitions.text: A reason for ill-feeling yet again

parts.words: A reason for ill-feeling yet again
parts.note: ill-feeling reads as resentment, but it means literally feeling ill, and doing so once more after a recovery

explanation.definitionFit: A relapse is a return of sickness after apparent recovery, which makes a patient feel unwell a second time.

clue.text: Transport as is right and fitting by river

parts.note: apt means suitable or fitting
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: Describing how goods are shipped properly and conveniently along a waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transport' looks like shipping, but here it is the noun meaning ecstasy. 'as is' and 'by' only join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Transport in the sense of being carried away by strong emotion is a synonym for ecstasy or bliss.

clue.text: A poet, though unfamiliar as yet

indicators.note: unfamiliar suggests something made strange, so the letters of the two words are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Remarking on a poet whose work one has not yet come across.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfamiliar' scrambles AS YET; 'though' only links. W. B. Yeats was the great Irish poet.
explanation.definitionFit: W. B. Yeats was an Irish writer of verse who won the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1923.

clue.text: Tears of the inexperienced person one criticizes

parts.note: L stands for learner, as on the L-plates of a new driver
an ace is the card counting as one
to rate someone is to scold or berate them

explanation.surface: Weeping of a novice who keeps finding fault with others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tears' reads as weeping but is the verb meaning rips. ACE as one comes from cards and dice.
explanation.definitionFit: To lacerate is to rip or gash flesh, so the third-person verb matches rips.

clue.text: He may stop playing!

parts.note: stop seems to mean cease, but a stop is a knob on a church instrument that brings in a set of pipes, so this player pulls one while performing

explanation.definitionFit: A church musician at the keyboard of a pipe instrument pulls out stops to change the sound while playing.

clue.text: They are in charge of wards

definitions.text: They are in charge of wards

parts.words: They are in charge of wards
parts.note: wards suggest hospital wards and nurses, but a ward is also a child under someone's legal protection

explanation.definitionFit: Legal protectors look after minors placed under their care by a court.

clue.text: Pound note remains

parts.note: B is one of the musical notes
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A banknote worth a pound is all that is left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' looks like the currency, with 'note' backing that up, but it is the verb meaning to strike hard.
explanation.definitionFit: To pound something is to hit it heavily and repeatedly, the same as a heavy blow.

clue.text: "The evening star, Love's" (Milton)

parts.note: a missing word completes a line of Paradise Lost, where the evening star is called the forerunner of love

explanation.walkthrough: The page prints a dash after 'Love's' for the missing word: Milton wrote 'The evening star, Love's harbinger'.
explanation.definitionFit: A herald or forerunner announces something to come, as the evening star announces the hour of love.

clue.text: Sad outcome of rent reduction

parts.note: a rent is a rip or tear
a drop is a fall or reduction

explanation.surface: The unhappy result of a rent cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' reads as money paid to a landlord; it is a rip.
explanation.definitionFit: A single drop of weeping falls when someone is unhappy.

clue.text: Get up late!

parts.note: looks like advice to lie in, but get up means dig up and the late means a dead person

explanation.definitionFit: To exhume a corpse is to dig it up from its grave.

clue.text: Leaves many a bird

parts.note: tea is made from the dried leaves of a plant
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, taken as many

explanation.surface: Many a bird departs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb of departure; it is tea leaves. 'a' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: The teal is a small freshwater duck, a kind of waterfowl.

clue.text: Act in a less restrained way and cause confusion

definitions.text: Act in a less restrained way

explanation.surface: Behaving more wildly and so baffling people.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words, be wilder means behave more unruly; as one word it means to perplex or puzzle someone.

clue.text: A story told in parts: of Israel maybe

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters of the place could be ordered some other way

explanation.surface: A story in instalments about bits of Israel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges ISRAEL; 'of' only links. 'parts' suggests regions of the country but means instalments.
explanation.definitionFit: A tale published or broadcast in instalments over successive issues or episodes.

clue.text: Strain to find way about the ship

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
re means about or concerning
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Trying hard to find a route around the vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to find' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressure or tension, as on a material or a mind, is a synonym of strain.

clue.text: The kind of day Zinoviev might have written off?

definitions.text: The kind of day Zinoviev might have written off?

parts.words: The kind of day Zinoviev might have written off?
parts.note: a memorable day is described by a colour-coded phrase, and the Bolshevik Zinoviev was supposedly the author of a notorious letter, so a Communist missive fits the phrase

explanation.walkthrough: The Zinoviev letter was a forged 1924 document, attributed to the Soviet official Grigory Zinoviev, that damaged Britain's Labour Party; red is the colour of Communism.
explanation.definitionFit: A red-letter day is a special, memorable occasion, from the saints' days printed in red in old calendars.

clue.text: General carrying the sovereign's weapon.

indicators.note: carrying means holding within, so one word wraps around the other

parts.note: rife means widespread or general
a sovereign was a gold coin worth one pound, abbreviated L from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: An army general holding the monarch's gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' looks like a military rank; it is the adjective. A sovereign is an old British gold pound coin, and L stands for pound.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-barrelled firearm with a grooved bore is a soldier's standard gun.

clue.text: Old people need one nice break

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: to break something is to smash it, so the word nice is broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Elderly folk deserve a pleasant holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old people' suggests pensioners on a 'nice break', but it means an ancient tribe; 'break' rearranges NICE into CENI, and 'need' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iceni were an ancient British tribe of East Anglia, led by Boudicca against Rome.

clue.text: Are no longer first

parts.note: ex means former, no longer so
first written as a numeral is 1st, and the 1 is read as the letter I

explanation.surface: Things that are no longer in first place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Are' is the definition, a verb meaning to live or be.
explanation.definitionFit: To be is to have being, to live or be real, the plain verb of existence.

clue.text: Slight scrap in the queue

indicators.note: in places the scrap inside the line of people

parts.note: a file is a line of people one behind another
a rag is a scrap of cloth

explanation.surface: A minor fight breaks out among people waiting in line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrap' reads as a fight in a queue; it is a rag. 'Slight' is the adjective meaning frail.
explanation.definitionFit: Something slight in build is delicate and easily broken, the sense of frail.

clue.text: Telephone about the duck — dry and going bad

indicators.note: about means around, so the call surrounds the other letters

parts.note: to ring someone is to telephone them
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, which looks like the letter O
TT means teetotal, someone who stays off alcohol

explanation.surface: Calling about a duck that has been left to dry out and is going off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' only links. A duck in cricket is a batter's score of zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is decaying or decomposing is spoiling, the sense of going off.

clue.text: In speech, canvass support

parts.note: canvass seems to mean seeking votes, but spoken aloud it is the painter's cloth, and the thing holding that cloth up on a stand is meant

explanation.definitionFit: An artist's wooden stand holds a painting while it is worked on.

clue.text: Inset paragraph or it has a divisive effect

indicators.note: in tells us to put the abbreviation inside the word that follows

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An indented paragraph, or something else that splits a page apart.
explanation.walkthrough: The page runs 'In set' together as 'Inset', which looks like typographic jargon; 'In' puts PARA inside SET.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that divides things or keeps them apart has a dividing effect.
